**This is individual work.** Every student submits their own. The final project is where you work
in a team; the studio is where the mechanics get into your own hands.
:::

The session runs to a fixed clock: **Classify** 25 minutes, **Tool** 20, **Reconcile** 15, **peer
check** 5. The move from Classify to Tool is called at minute 30 whether or not you finished — an
unfinished classification is a legitimate finding, reported as one.

::: {.part}
### Part 1 · Before you arrive

Accounts and one install. Do this before Thursday, not during it.

1. Create a Taiga account at [tree.taiga.io](https://tree.taiga.io) with your NDSU email, and a private project named `IMSE456-yourlastname`.
2. Install [ProjectLibre](https://www.projectlibre.com/) and open it once to confirm it launches. If it fails on your machine it fails *today*, not in Week 4 — [GanttProject](https://www.ganttproject.biz/) is the sanctioned fallback and costs you nothing.
3. Create the cloud folder you will use all semester — Google Drive or OneDrive, named `IMSE456`. **Everything in this course is saved there, never to a local disk.**
4. Claim your AI access: register the free student year at [gemini.google/students](https://gemini.google/students/) if you are eligible. If you are not, the free Gemini tier is sufficient for every studio in this course — say so in your submission so it is on record.
5. Open the access form linked on Blackboard and answer both questions: which machine you will work on, and which AI tooling you can reach. Two minutes, no effect on your grade — it decides which version of every later lab sheet you get.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 2 · What you will have at the end

SA1 — your Taiga sandbox URL, your `.pod` file, the classification table for six initiatives, and
one paragraph naming a specific field.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 3 · Classify it yourself — 25 minutes

**You go first. The model goes second.** That order is the point of the exercise, and reversing it
costs you the only data the studio generates.

1. Pick a campus organization you actually know — a club, a lab, a team, an employer.
2. Write down **six** things it is currently doing or could do in the next year. Real ones.
3. Classify each as **project**, **operation**, or **hybrid** using the temporary-and-unique test. Write one sentence of justification for every one. No exceptions, including the obvious ones.
4. *Now* ask Gemini to generate six candidate initiatives for the same organization, and to classify them the same way.
5. Build the table: your six with your classifications, the model's six with its classifications. Mark every item where you and the model would disagree, and every model classification you judge **wrong**.

The disagreements are the deliverable. A table with no disagreements means one of you was not
paying attention, and it was probably not the model.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 4 · Now the professional tools — 20 minutes

1. Take the three items you classified as **projects**. Enter them into your Taiga sandbox as epics.
2. Enter the same three into ProjectLibre as summary tasks with placeholder durations. Save as `SA1_yourlastname.pod`.
3. Write down what each tool **forced** you to state that the other did not. Be specific — name the field, not the feeling.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 5 · Where do they disagree? — 15 minutes

Which tool made you commit to something you did not yet know?

One paragraph, naming the **specific field**. "ProjectLibre wanted a duration" is the beginning of
an answer; "ProjectLibre would not let me save a task without a duration, so I invented three days
for something I have never done" is the answer.

**This is the graded part** — it is the only thing here a machine cannot check for you.
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 6 · Done looks like — the checklist your neighbour runs on you at minute 70

- [ ] Taiga account created and the sandbox project exists, with three epics in it
- [ ] ProjectLibre opens on your machine, or you have reported the failure and used GanttProject
- [ ] AI access claimed, or reported
- [ ] six items classified by you, each with a written justification
- [ ] the model's six classified too, with disagreements marked
- [ ] the paragraph names a specific field
:::

::: {.part}
### Part 7 · Where it is saved

`IMSE456/studio-01/` in your cloud folder. Name files `SA1_yourlastname.*`.

**Nothing in this course is saved to a local disk.** Lab machines wipe on reboot and laptops get
left at home. Submit the PDF to Blackboard by the due date above.
:::

::: {.browser-path}
**Working on lab machines?**

**No ProjectLibre?** Do the *Tool* half in Smartsheet instead — indented WBS, Gantt, predecessors
and critical path all work in a browser. Export to PDF in place of the `.pod`. Say so in your

:::

## Study loop for this week

Run this before you read the notes, and again after. It is not graded; it is the fastest way to find
out what you have wrong.

```text
Be my tutor on what "project success" means and why it's contested. Ask me
one question at a time. Don't lecture. Start by making me define success,
then attack my definition. Push until I admit it's multidimensional, then
make me name the dimensions myself.
```

See [AI Studio](../ai.qmd) for the Editor and Roommate prompts and the full loop.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Label it, verify it, own it.** Append the AI acknowledgement block from the [syllabus](../syllabus.qmd#how-to-disclose): the tool, the prompt or transcript link, what you changed after reviewing its output, and what it got wrong. Every quantitative result arrives with the check that proves it — **the check is graded, not the output**. "The model said so" is not a defence in this course or in a project review.
:::
